title: Set up by the door
note:
Written after the fact, like door-sound-02-self: this is one of the eight scenes drawn by hand before the pipeline existed. It is being redrawn for the door's window only — the set was split 3–3 and four panes won, being both what the live brief says and what is physically true of one door seen from either side — so everything else about the picture is reconstructed to survive unchanged.

This and door-sound-02-self are a near-duplicate pair and always will be: same hall, same camera, same standing handler cropped at the top of the frame, same sitting dog, same leash under the same shoe. The ONE thing that separates them is the arms. Here both hands hang empty and relaxed at her sides and nothing is raised; in 02-self her near fist is up at the door frame, knocking. The tan-era brief put it as 'the single thing this image must make obvious: the leash is trapped under the foot and both hands are free', and that is still the claim.

Round 13 got the arms, the trapped leash and the window right and still had to be redrawn: Lucy was looking up at the handler's face, which is the read of door-sound-03-name one picture later in the same activity. The post-mortems are explicit that a gaze has to be specified as the whole muzzle pointed at a named thing, positioned relative to her head — an adjective like 'attentive' does not steer it — so the door is now named as being off to her right with her head level.
scene: Interior entry hall, beside the closed charcoal front door, which stands on the right of the frame. Match attachment 1 exactly for the room, the camera height, the distance from the viewer, the wall, the floor, the baseboard, the door and the doormat: this is the same hall in the moment just before it, and only the handler's arms differ. The handler is cropped by the TOP of the frame at the shoulders, so only her body from the shoulders down is in the picture — her head is not visible, and that crop is deliberate and must be kept. She stands square and still beside Lucy, facing the door, weight even on both feet. BOTH OF HER HANDS ARE EMPTY, open, and hanging relaxed at her sides. Nothing is raised, nothing is reaching, neither hand is near the door, the door frame or the treat pouch, and there is no treat anywhere in the picture. Lucy sits square on the floor at the handler's side, close against her leg, calm and settled, ears up and attentive. HER WHOLE MUZZLE POINTS AT THE CLOSED DOOR, off to her right and across the frame from her, with her head level rather than tilted up. She is watching the door, waiting for something to happen there. She must NOT be looking up at the handler or at the handler's face or hands: a dog checking in with her handler is door-sound-03-name, a different picture in this same activity, and these two must not read as each other. The black leash is clipped to the ring on Lucy's collar at the front of her neck, runs down and forward, and passes UNDER the handler's near shoe, with a loose loop of slack lying on the oak floor — the trapped leash is the point of this picture and must be unmistakable. THE DOOR'S WINDOW: a four-pane grid in the upper half of the door — two panes across and two panes down, divided by one vertical bar and one horizontal bar, pale spruce foliage beyond. Four panes, in this and in every other picture of this door. Background: the closed charcoal door with its four-pane window, the woven doormat, one baseboard line, the lavender-grey wall, the oak floor. Nothing else in the room.
mustBeTrue: the leash runs from Lucy's collar down and under the handler's near shoe with a visible loop of slack, both of the handler's hands are empty and hanging relaxed at her sides with nothing raised and nothing reaching, the door's window is a four-pane grid, and Lucy sits square and close at the handler's side with her whole muzzle pointed at the closed door and her head level, not looking up at the handler.
